content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions involving nevirapine and other medications, focusing on the effects of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. 1. Laroctrectinib and Nevirapine: Laroctrectinib may increase the levels or effects of nevirapine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Nevirapine and Lemborexant: Nevirapine can increase the levels or effects of lemborexant via CYP3A4 metabolism. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. 3. Lenacapavir and Nevirapine: Lenacapavir may decrease the levels or effects of nevirapine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended due to the potential loss of therapeutic efficacy and the risk of resistance development. 4. Letermovir and Nevirapine: Letermovir increases nevirapine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Levoketoconazole and Nevirapine: Levoketoconazole increases nevirapine levels, while nevirapine decreases levoketoconazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Nevirapine and Levonorgestrel (Intrauterine or Oral): Nevirapine reduces levonorgestrel levels, potentially decreasing contraceptive efficacy. Alternative or backup contraception is recommended during and for 28 days after discontinuing nevirapine. 7. Nevirapine and Lidocaine: Nevirapine decreases lidocaine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Nevirapine and Linagliptin: Nevirapine reduces linagliptin levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia due to potential insulin resistance. 9. Nevirapine and Lomitapide: Nevirapine increases lomitapide levels. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. Monitor closely. 10. Nevirapine and Lonafarnib: Nevirapine increases lonafarnib levels, which may lead to arrhythmias. Co-administration is not recommended. If unavoidable, reduce lonafarnib to the starting dose and monitor for cardiac events. 11. Nevirapine and Lopinavir: Nevirapine decreases lopinavir levels, while lopinavir increases nevirapine levels. Co-administration is not recommended due to the risk of reduced efficacy. 12. Nevirapine and Loratadine: Nevirapine decreases loratadine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Nevirapine and Lorlatinib: Lorlatinib decreases nevirapine levels, increasing the risk of severe hepatotoxicity. Co-administration is not recommended. 14. Nevirapine and Losartan: Nevirapine reduces losartan levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Nevirapine and Lovastatin: Nevirapine decreases lovastatin levels. Co-administration is not recommended. 16. Nevirapine and Lovotibeglogene Autotemcel: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. ART may interfere with the manufacturing of lovotibeglogene autotemcel. 17. Nevirapine and Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Nevirapine decreases ivacaftor exposure, reducing its effectiveness. Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Nevirapine and Lumefantrine: Nevirapine reduces lumefantrine levels, potentially leading to loss of antimalarial efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Nevirapine and Lurasidone: Nevirapine decreases lurasidone levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Nevirapine and Macimorelin: Nevirapine reduces macimorelin levels, potentially causing false-positive test results. Discontinue strong CYP3A4 inducers before testing. 21. Nevirapine and Macitentan: Nevirapine decreases macitentan levels. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 22. Nevirapine and Maraviroc: Nevirapine reduces maraviroc levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Nevirapine and Medroxyprogesterone: Nevirapine decreases medroxyprogesterone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Nevirapine and Mefloquine: Nevirapine reduces mefloquine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Nevirapine and Meloxicam: Nevirapine decreases meloxicam levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Nevirapine and Meperidine: Nevirapine reduces meperidine levels, increasing toxic metabolite formation. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Nevirapine and Mestranol: Nevirapine decreases mestranol levels, reducing contraceptive efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Nevirapine and Methadone: Nevirapine decreases methadone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Nevirapine and Methylprednisolone: Nevirapine reduces methylprednisolone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Nevirapine and Midazolam: Nevirapine decreases midazolam levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Intranasal midazolam may have prolonged sedation due to increased systemic exposure. 31. Nevirapine and Midostaurin: Nevirapine reduces midostaurin levels, potentially decreasing efficacy. Co-administration is not recommended. 32. Nevirapine and Mifepristone: Nevirapine decreases mifepristone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Nevirapine and Mirtazapine: Nevirapine reduces mirtazapine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Mitotane and Nevirapine: Mitotane decreases nevirapine levels. Monitor closely for dosage adjustments. 35. Nevirapine and Modafinil: Nevirapine reduces modafinil levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Nevirapine and Montelukast: Nevirapine decreases montelukast levels. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 37. Nafcillin and Nevirapine: Nafcillin decreases nevirapine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Nevirapine and Naldemedine: Nevirapine reduces naldemedine levels. Co-administration is not recommended. 39. Nevirapine and Naloxegol: Nevirapine decreases naloxegol levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 40. Nevirapine and Nateglinide: Nevirapine reduces nateglinide levels. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 41. Nevirapine and Nefazodone: Nevirapine decreases nefazodone levels, while nefazodone increases nevirapine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 42. Nevirapine and Nelfinavir: Nevirapine decreases nelfinavir levels, and both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Nevirapine and Neratnib: Nevirapine reduces neratinib levels. Co-administration is not recommended. 44. Nevirapine and Netupitant/Palonosetron: Nevirapine decreases netupitant levels. Co-administration is not recommended. 45. Nevirapine and Nicardipine: Nevirapine reduces nicardipine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Nevirapine and Nifedipine: Nevirapine decreases nifedipine levels. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 47. Nevirapine and Nilotinib: Nevirapine reduces nilotinib levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Nevirapine and Nimodipine: Nevirapine decreases nimodipine levels. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 49. Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir and Nevirapine: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases nevirapine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Nevirapine and Nisoldipine: Nevirapine reduces nisoldipine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Nevirapine and Nitrendipine: Nevirapine decreases nitrendipine levels. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 52. Nevirapine and Olaparib: Nevirapine reduces olaparib levels. Co-administration is not recommended. 53. Nevirapine and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir & Dasabuvir: Nevirapine decreases drug levels, reducing efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 54. Nevirapine and Ondansetron: Nevirapine decreases ondansetron levels. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 55. Orlistat and Nevirapine: Orlistat reduces nevirapine absorption, potentially leading to virological failure. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 56. Nevirapine and Osilodrostat: Nevirapine decreases osilodrostat levels. Adjust osilodrostat dosage if necessary and monitor closely. 57. Nevirapine and Osimertinib: Nevirapine reduces osimertinib levels. Co-administration is not recommended. 58. Nevirapine and Ospemifene: Nevirapine decreases ospemifene levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Oxcarbazepine and Nevirapine: Oxcarbazepine decreases nevirapine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Nevirapine and Oxybutynin: Nevirapine reduces oxybutynin levels. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 61. Nevirapine and Oxycodone: Nevirapine decreases oxycodone levels. Use caution and monitor closely.
